subject.title: [Bug] web_fetch fails in dual-stack networks when DNS returns IPv6 special-use addresses

question: Should OpenClaw change the default SSRF DNS-answer rule from fail on any blocked resolved address to filter blocked candidates and proceed when at least one allowed address remains?
rationale: The implementation shape is narrow, but the default governs outbound requests under polluted or hostile DNS answers, so automation should not choose the SSRF boundary.

options.title: Approve filtered mixed-answer semantics
options.body: Allow mixed DNS result sets only after removing every blocked candidate from the pinned address pool, with tests for mixed-allowed and all-blocked results.

options.title: Keep any-blocked fail-closed
options.body: Treat any blocked DNS answer as an intentional stop and document trusted proxy or fake-IP opt-in settings as the supported workaround.

options.title: Make this opt-in
options.body: Preserve the current default and add or reuse an explicit operator-controlled policy for DNS-polluted environments.

recommendation.title: Approve filtered mixed-answer semantics
recommendation.body: Allow mixed DNS result sets only after removing every blocked candidate from the pinned address pool, with tests for mixed-allowed and all-blocked results.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest visible history in the SSRF host/IP and IPv6 special-use security boundary.
